headlines.title: 1 dead, 6 injured in mass shooting at pop-up party near Morgan Hill
headlines.description: Detectives are searching for answers and asking witnesses to come forward after a deadly mass shooting at a pop-up birthday party near Morgan Hill left one person dead and six others injured over the weekend. Family members identified the person killed as Desi Romero, known to loved ones as “Pepper.” An online fundraiser created to help pay for funeral expenses described Romero as a cherished son, brother, grandson, cousin and friend who had a way of bringing joy to everyone around him. “Pepper was taken from us far too soon, and our hearts are shattered,” the family wrote in the fundraiser. His grandfather noted that Romero once played for Evergreen Little League. In a statement, an acquaintance from his Little League days remembered him fondly. “He was a pleasure to watch on the field… and was always one of the most talented players — if not the most talented player — on the field,” the statement read. The unsanctioned Saturday night party was hosted by a Bay Area streamer in a field in an unincorporated area near Morgan Hill. Investigators estimate about 300 people attended the event. “This was sort of a pop-up party that was advertised on social media,” said Brooks Jarosz of the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office. “The location of that party was not given out until hours before the event occurred.” One woman who attended the party told NBC Bay Area there was security present and that men were being patted down before entering. However, she said one man somehow got past security with a handgun. “The guy who had the gun snuck in,” the woman said. “I don’t know how he did. Everyone saw that he had a gun, and then he got mad.” What was supposed to be a birthday celebration quickly ended in tragedy when gunfire erupted. Along with Romero’s death, six others suffered gunshot wounds. “For some it was the stomach, one in the ankle, one in the shoulder,” Jarosz said. “I can report now that four of the six who were injured are still in the hospital.” The sheriff’s office confirmed the shooter used a handgun, but investigators have not yet said whether they believe the shooting was targeted or if there is any gang connection. While investigators have already interviewed more than a dozen people, they are urging many more to come forward to help piece together what led up to the violence. “We want to talk to more so we can see if all of those stories match up and get a clear understanding of what happened,” Jarosz said. Authorities are asking anyone who attended the party, or who has photos or video from that night, to contact the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office.

headlines.title: Dangerous rip currents, sneaker waves prompt beach warnings along Bay Area coast
headlines.description: The National Weather Service has issued a Beach Hazards Statement for much of the Bay Area, warning of dangerous rip currents and sneaker waves that officials say should make visitors think twice before getting in the water. The warning comes just days after a dramatic weekend rescue at Seabright Beach in Santa Cruz, where a state lifeguard pulled a 10-year-old to safety after the child was caught in pounding surf. With dangerous conditions expected across the entire Bay Area coast on Tuesday, firefighters say the Santa Cruz incident is exactly the kind of situation they hope to prevent. At San Francisco’s Ocean Beach — an area already known for its dangerous surf — officials say the forecast could make an already unforgiving stretch of coastline even more hazardous. “We are urging caution to go out there,” San Francisco Fire Department spokesperson Samuel Menchaca said. “Don’t go out in the water, view from a distance if you can just due to some of those conditions being so intense right now.” Fire crews were out at Ocean Beach sharpening their beach rescue skills ahead of the forecasted hazards. “That way when the real thing comes they will be that much more prepared to execute that rescue,” Menchaca said. For visitors like Luis Gomez and Perla Hernandez, who are in town from Phoenix, the warning is enough to keep them on shore. “Especially because we have kids and we want nothing to happen to them,” Gomez said. “It’s dangerous and as a mother I would probably try to avoid a situation like that myself,” Hernandez added. As crews prepare for the possibility of water rescues, they are asking beachgoers to do their part by putting safety first. “Our number one tip that we always tell everyone… never turn your back on the ocean,” Menchaca said. The Beach Hazards Statement warns of rip currents and sneaker waves through Wednesday, and remains in effect through Saturday. Firefighters noted that even if visitors have no plans to swim, sneaker waves can rush much farther up the beach than people expect. Their advice: Enjoy the view from a safe distance, and if you don’t need to be near the water, consider staying away from the shoreline until conditions improve.

headlines.title: Tech giants launch open AI safety plan following breach
headlines.description: As new fears about the potential dangers of artificial intelligence mount, a group of Silicon Valley tech giants is coming together to try to make AI safer and more transparent. Shortly after AI agents from OpenAI hacked into another company’s systems to find information without anyone knowing, several tech companies, led by Nvidia, announced a new plan to make AI safer by being more open. At Nvidia headquarters, Kari Briski, vice president of generative AI software, said more transparent AI models and software will make the technology easier to inspect, track and defend. “When something is open you can inspect it, you can understand it,” Briski said. By making the framework open, developers hope to give users more control over the rapidly evolving technology. “So that you can not only recreate and understand and inspect what’s inside of this AI, but you can also use it to wield on your own terms,” Briski said. However, some security trackers say it may be too late, warning that the recent AI breach could have been much worse. J.B. Branch, director of AI governance at Public Citizen, called the situation a “historic moment.” “This could hack stock markets, this could hack biosecurity or nuclear weapons, or things along those lines,” Branch said. “This is just a low-level stakes example of what we mean when we say these products are able to cause risks that are unknowable or uncontrollable.” Despite these warnings, AI companies maintain they will work on safety first. When asked if the new initiative could lead to more trust when it comes to AI, Briski was optimistic. “I think so,” Briski said. “That’s absolutely part of the goal.”

headlines.title: 1 killed, 2 injured in early morning San Jose shooting
headlines.description: One man was killed and two others were injured in an early morning shooting Sunday that marks San Jose’s 16th homicide this year, authorities said. San Jose police officers responded to a report of a shooting in the area of Seventh Street and Leo Avenue at approximately 2:55 a.m. on July 26. Upon arrival, officers located two men suffering from at least one gunshot wound each, according to the San Jose Police Department. Despite lifesaving measures, one victim was pronounced dead at the scene. The second man was transported to a local hospital in critical condition and was later stabilized. Simultaneously, officers observed a vehicle traveling at a high rate of speed near 11th Street and Humboldt Street. Officers conducted an enforcement stop and discovered a third man inside the vehicle who was also suffering from at least one gunshot wound. He was transported to a local hospital for treatment, and his injuries were later determined to be non-life-threatening. The SJPD’s Homicide Unit responded to the scene and is investigating the incident. The motive and circumstances surrounding the shooting remain under investigation. Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact Detective Sgt. Barragan (badge No. 4106) or Detective Harrington (badge No. 4365) of the SJPD’s Homicide Unit via email at 4106@sanjoseca.gov or 4365@sanjoseca.gov, or by calling 408-277-5283. Anonymous tips can be submitted using the P3TIPS mobile app, by calling the tip line at 408-947-STOP, or online at www.siliconvalleycrimestoppers.org. Information leading to an arrest may be eligible for a cash reward from the Silicon Valley Crime Stoppers Program.

headlines.title: Beach hazard warning issued for Bay Area coastline
headlines.description: The National Weather Service has issued a beach hazard warning for most of the Bay Area, stretching from Sonoma County to Monterey, as Pacific storm activity churns up the risk of sneaker waves and strong rip currents. The statement, which remains in effect until Wednesday, follows a weekend of dangerous conditions. Authorities are pointing to a dramatic video from Seabright Beach in Santa Cruz — where a state beach lifeguard is seen hanging onto a 10-year-old in the rough surf — as exactly the type of situation they want the public to avoid. In response to the hazard, the San Francisco Fire Department conducted a previously scheduled beach rescue training near the Golden Gate Bridge that proved especially timely. “It may not be that deep but it can still pull you around and pull you down,” San Francisco Fire Department spokesperson Samuel Machaca said. “That lifeguard did a great job. We don’t want to see that here in San Francisco, we want everyone to be safe.” Along Ocean Beach, beach patrols kept a close eye out for any trouble. Only a couple of surfers were spotted in the water, which Machaca noted is a pretty good indication that the waves are too choppy and not worth the risk. San Francisco resident Sally Magnuson said it was a nice day to feel the warm sand, but not to get in the water. “For me, I know that Ocean Beach is a little bit more aggressive,” Magnuson said. “And I wouldn’t like, bring my friends from out of town to experience the Pacific here.” However, Sam Clode and his friends, visiting from North Carolina, really wanted to be in the Pacific and decided to brave the surf. “It was fun,” Clode said. “I can see why people should maybe be a little hesitant. But, I think if you’re a little more experienced, it shouldn’t be too terrible.” For those who do want to venture to any beach during the advisory, the fire department recommends traveling in pairs or a group so someone can call for help in an emergency. “If there is an emergency and you are down on the beach, know where you are, what stairwell you came in on, what cross street location,” Machaca said.

headlines.title: California DOJ investigates fatal Fremont police shooting
headlines.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced Monday that the California Department of Justice is investigating the circumstances that led to a police officer fatally shooting an allegedly armed suspect on Friday in Fremont. The shooting, which resulted in the death of one individual, happened at approximately 3:38 p.m. on July 24 at an assisted living facility on Walnut Avenue, according to the Fremont Police Department. Following notification of the incident, the DOJ’s California Police Shooting Investigation Team initiated an investigation in accordance with Assembly Bill 1506 mandates. Upon completion, the investigation will be turned over to the DOJ’s Special Prosecutions Section within the Criminal Law Division for an independent review. Anyone who has information related to the incident is asked to report it by calling 916-210-2871.

headlines.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan recovering from serious car crash as training camp opens
headlines.description: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan is recovering from a serious car crash he had two weeks ago, just as training camp officially gets underway. Shanahan suffered a concussion, a broken nose, broken ribs and a broken hand in a two-car crash in Palo Alto on July 14. The team kept the accident under wraps until the start of training camp Sunday. Palo Alto police are still investigating the incident, saying no drugs or alcohol were involved and that both drivers are cooperating. At Levi’s Stadium, star players and fans were out for practice. Shanahan was missing during the first half, as his work schedule is being limited by his injuries. He later appeared on the field for less than an hour as the team monitored his concussion symptoms. His hand appeared to be in a bandage, but he was seen taking notes and talking to players. Quarterback Brock Purdy said he reached out to Shanahan when he found out about the accident. “I shot him a text after I heard the news. And we talked back and forth,” Purdy said. “Just saw him on the field for the first time. Hugged him. Told him I loved him.” Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir noted the impact of having Shanahan present at practice despite his injuries. “You still gotta show up and perform,” Lenoir said. “You want to give it your best because your head coach is watching.” Fans were excited to see their favorite players out on the field. George Kittle is also injured, but the tight end still ran to give fans a show. “I love you man. Holy crap. This is crazy. Yes, George. Let’s go! Thank you so much,” one fan cheered. Some fans said it was good just to see the coach on the field for a bit, knowing everything is going to be OK. “It was amazing, I hope he has a great recovery,” 49ers fan Ron Lardizabar said.

headlines.title: Aggressive Mines Fire grows in Santa Clara County, Cal Fire says
headlines.description: The Mines Fire burning in Santa Clara County has grown with a dangerous rate of spread, Cal Fire said Monday. The fire, which was first reported just after 2 p.m. on Sunday, has now burned 283 acres. On Sunday night, CalFire said crews had halted the fire’s progression, and it had been holding at 40% containment through Monday. But by Monday afternoon, authorities said the aggressive blaze had spread. So far no structures are threatened. The fire is centralized near Mines and San Antonio Valley roads in the San Antone Valley. The cause of the fire is still under investigation. Aug 19, 2020 Santa Clara County Jul 26 Northern California Jul 26 Evacuations underway as firefighters battle fire in Tuolumne County

headlines.title: Police investigating shooting in San Francisco
headlines.description: Police are investigating a shooting Monday afternoon in San Francisco. The incident was reported just before 3 p.m. in the area of Market and Jones streets when officers patrolling the area heard gunshots. “Officers searched the area and discovered that a victim had been shot and the suspect fled the scene on foot,” police said in a new release. The victim was taken to a hospital for life-threatening injuries. Anyone with information is asked to contact SFPD at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411 and begin the message with SFPD. No other information was immediately available. San Francisco Jul 26 San Francisco Jul 25 San Francisco 12 hours ago Project Open Hand marks 30 million meals served in San Francisco

headlines.title: San Jose police arrest 3, recover 3 firearms in series of vehicle stops
headlines.description: San Jose police arrested three suspects and recovered three firearms—including a stolen gun and a privately made weapon—during a series of separate vehicle stops over a two-day span. The first incident occurred Friday at approximately 1:17 a.m. Central Division patrol officers stopped a reported stolen vehicle with three occupants inside. According to police, the driver was operating the vehicle under the influence and was found in possession of both a firearm and narcotics. The driver was arrested and booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail for multiple crimes, including firearm and narcotics-related offenses. The following day, at approximately 1:13 a.m., Central Division officers conducted another vehicle enforcement stop. During the investigation, police located a loaded firearm that was confirmed to be stolen. A passenger in the vehicle was arrested and booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail. Later that evening, at approximately 6 p.m., officers with the San Jose Police Department’s Special Operations Division conducted a third vehicle stop. Officers observed multiple open containers of alcohol inside the car, prompting a probable cause search. During the search, police found a privately made firearm on one of the passengers. That suspect was also booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail for various firearm-related crimes.

headlines.title: Loved ones mourn young man who was fatally shot at party near Morgan Hill
headlines.description: A young man who was shot and killed Saturday night at a pop-up birthday party near Morgan Hill is being remembered by loved ones as a “cherished son, brother, grandson, cousin, and friend.” Desi Romero, also known as “Pepper,” was shot to death in the area of Hale and Miramonte avenues during a party hosted by a Bay Area livestreamer. Six other people were injured. In a GoFundMe page, loved ones said, “Pepper was taken from us far too soon, and our hearts are shattered.” The Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office said about 300 people attended the party, which was held in a field. “This was sort of a pop-up party that was advertised on social media,” Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office spokesperson Brooks Jarosz said. “The location of that party was not given out until hours before the event occurred. Hundreds of people showed up in what is more or less a field on Hale Avenue in unincorporated Morgan Hill.” The shooter remained at large as of Monday evening. People who were at the party said a man with a gun got past private security and opened fire. “The guy that had the gun snuck in,” a woman in attendance said. “I don’t know how, but I guess he had a gun. Everyone seen that he did, and then he got mad.” A fight then broke out, the woman said. “I guess they were arguing and that’s when everybody started running and they heard gunshots,” the woman said. While some partygoers said they believe the shooting was gang related, the sheriff’s office said it could not immediately confirm that. Deputies spent Monday interviewing witnesses and confirmed the shooter used a handgun. Detectives asked anyone who was at the party to reach out to the sheriff’s office.

headlines.title: Nonprofit to distribute free school supplies to thousands of Bay Area students
headlines.description: Back-to-school shopping can trigger sticker shock for many parents, but thousands of local students will benefit from a local group that started distributing free school supplies on Monday. Family Giving Tree volunteers are preparing backpacks and supplies for 35,000 students across the greater Bay Area region, covering 12 counties and 250 schools. “There are just so many more expenses and costs to everything that it makes it just really hard for folks to be able to fill a backpack for a student for their first day of school,” Family Giving Tree Resource Director Evelyn Huynh said. “Upwards of $100 just for a basic backpack with all the supplies needed for a grade. It can really add up.” Family Giving Tree will be accepting back-to-school donations until Friday at public drive-up locations. Donors can also bring supplies directly to its headquarters at any time.
